aspects.title: R4 joint partition sum
aspects.question: Was the correct joint partition sum evaluated, with sums separated by logical sector?
aspects.why_it_matters: Optimal logical decoding compares the total posterior mass of the two logical sectors. Separating the shared edge orientation, or finding only the single most likely error, changes the probability model specified in the problem.
possible_mistakes: Sample the orientation at the two endpoints of the same edge independently.
Replace the global joint sum with vertex-by-vertex local likelihoods.
Treat the MAP microscopic configuration as the logical-sector posterior.
Omit the top-boundary logical parity.
aspects.observed_summary: All seven submissions retain three-state edge variables 0,+,- and carry logical parity to compute Z0,Z1; none of these modeling errors was found in the checked cases. Using two states in O0/SU2 special cases where orientations can be eliminated exactly is a valid optimization.
aspects.conclusion: All seven receive the same score here; the main differences concern extreme numerical range and evidence for larger-size approximations, rather than the partition-sum definition.

aspects.title: R4 exact algorithm
aspects.question: Does the prescribed small-size regime L≤4,N≤8 use an exact or certified algorithm?
aspects.why_it_matters: The small-size exact API is an automatically checkable deliverable. The algorithm should retain all configurations. Its complexity may grow exponentially with width, without first proving that the model is free fermionic.
possible_mistakes: Call a truncated MPS result an untruncated exact result.
Conflate a large-size approximation with the prescribed small-size API.
Substitute an unimplemented Pfaffian/free-fermion theory for a working algorithm.
aspects.observed_summary: All seven prescribed small-size APIs use untruncated frontier/transfer-matrix summation. The Opus large-size MPS computations are separate approximations; their error claims are scored in A3 and are not penalized twice here.
aspects.conclusion: All satisfy the original small-size algorithm requirement. Opus02's public API switches to MPS at L>9, so exactness claims must specify the size range.

aspects.title: R4 numerical range
aspects.question: Can the posterior of a legal record still be evaluated at extremely small but positive probabilities?
aspects.why_it_matters: Z0 and Z1 may both be tiny while their ratio remains defined. Stepwise normalization cannot restore edge weights or local products that have already underflowed to zero.
possible_mistakes: Misreport numerical underflow as a zero-probability record.
Normalize only after each column, after already forming extremely small products in ordinary float arithmetic.
Use a dtype name instead of checking the floating-point range across platforms.
aspects.observed_summary: All seven pass routine cases. On 18 additional extremely low-p positive-probability stress cases, all three GPT runs pass, whereas Fable03 and all three Opus runs do not. Existing rubric scores are retained, with the macOS/Linux longdouble difference noted.
aspects.conclusion: This item reveals a substantive posterior-API difference: GPT's high-precision or log-domain fallback covers the checked domain; the other four have numerical-underflow gaps.

aspects.title: decode interface
aspects.question: Does decode return a legal correction and choose the maximum-posterior logical sector?
aspects.why_it_matters: Correct posterior values are insufficient: the output must be an edge set in the specified geometry, satisfy Hc=s, and have logical parity consistent with the posterior decision. Either sector is valid at a tie.
possible_mistakes: Output edges outside the geometry.
Return only a logical bit without constructing a correction.
Construct a correction with the correct syndrome but wrong logical parity.
Treat the correction as a microscopic configuration that must recover the true arrows.
aspects.observed_summary: On 210 routine cases, all seven corrections are legal, have the correct syndrome, and agree with the reference maximum-posterior logical sector; extreme numerical failures already scored in D4 are not penalized again here.
aspects.conclusion: The routine decode interface does not distinguish the seven submissions; these checks do not validate the large-size phase-diagram limit.

aspects.title: Data/unconditional accounting
aspects.question: Are all attempts, exceptions, stopping rules and raw data accounted for unconditionally?
aspects.why_it_matters: Dropping difficult records biases risk downward. The exception-as-failure rule must enter the reported metrics; reserved slots must not be presented as completed physical trials.
possible_mistakes: Remove exceptional samples from the denominator.
Assign hard failure 1 but posterior-min risk only 0.5.
Save only successful posterior evaluations, preventing selection-bias auditing.
Report the reserved slots of an externally terminated batch as completed trials.

Fable03 has a latent half-failure exception-accounting defect, but zero archived exceptions; Opus01 reports 2 actual exceptions, and all three Opus codes assign exception risk 0.5 and hard failure 1. GPT conservatively assigns 1; GPT03 explicitly discloses 200 reserved slots.
aspects.conclusion: Distinguish risk estimation from hard failure: the task requires exceptions to count as failures, so both should receive 1. Fable's issue has not affected saved estimates; Opus01 has actual triggering records.

algorithm_comparison.question: How does each run compute the partition function, and what are its exact and approximate ranges?

rows.exact_small_L: Exact three-state frontier transfer matrix, with two-state special cases where appropriate.
rows.large_L_method: The study uses exact contraction: three-state L≤12, two-state L≤16, without MPS truncation.
rows.limit: Exact up to rounding; external small-size checks pass, but do not validate infinite-size extrapolation.

rows.exact_small_L: Untruncated column transfer matrix with explicit logical parity.
rows.large_L_method: The report states exact ternary L≤14 and binary L≤18; larger sizes through L48 use χ64 MPS.
rows.limit: The χ64/128 difference is an empirical stability check, not a rigorous bound on true bias; see A3.

rows.exact_small_L: The public API uses an exact frontier at L≤9; L≤4 satisfies R4.
rows.large_L_method: The public API uses χ64 MPS at L>9; production scans also use χ32/48 and other settings.
rows.limit: API and study-scan parameters differ; the README's broad exactness wording does not cover L>9.

rows.exact_small_L: The public small-size API uses an exact frontier, with valid elimination in two-state special cases.
rows.large_L_method: Exploration at L≤12 uses exact inference; production Q2—Q9 use χ64 MPS at all L, with some χ128 checks.
rows.limit: Truncation weights and χ comparisons are present; these do not automatically certify every production posterior's error.

rows.exact_small_L: Untruncated three-state column frontier with Decimal fallback.
rows.large_L_method: Dense and exact sparse support storage; sparsification uses no weight threshold.
rows.limit: Deleting zero support in an exact storage variant is not approximate truncation; large-size limits still require extrapolation or theorems.

rows.exact_small_L: Nonnegative exact column summation, with log-domain inference near endpoints.
rows.large_L_method: compressed.py performs exact support pruning and removes no positive-weight configurations.
rows.limit: Memory is exponential in width; MPS or free fermions are not needed to satisfy the small-size requirement.

rows.exact_small_L: Exact column-frontier summation with log arithmetic for extremely small probabilities.
rows.large_L_method: The study uses the same kind of exact frontier, without MPS truncation.
rows.limit: The archived study has reserved slots from external termination; exact summation does not mean every planned trial ran.

algorithm_comparison.conclusion: All seven core methods are finite-width tensor/transfer contractions; none requires a free-fermion mapping to complete R4. Opus03 discusses a Pfaffian route, but its implementation uses transfer/MPS. R4 small-size exact inference and R1 large-size approximation must be assessed in separate columns.

verification_scope.stress_parameters: L=2,3,4; N=8; O1/O2; p=1e-180,1e-310,and the smallest positive float 5e-324.
verification_scope.routine_result: All seven pass 210/210 posterior and decode checks; this is not exhaustive validation of all legal records.
verification_scope.oracle_independence: The existing reference uses independent geometry, irrep construction and generic einsum; 21 L2 cases are additionally compared with microscopic enumeration, with maximum difference 8.67e-19.
verification_scope.platform_caveat: Stress validation runs on macOS. np.longdouble may have a different exponent range from the original Linux environment, so not all macOS failures can be extrapolated directly to that environment. Opus02 computes edge-weight p/2 in Python float before conversion to dtype; rounding to zero at the smallest positive float is a cross-platform issue.
verification_scope.resource_limit: Only the submitted 8CPU/32GiB/no-GPU records and existing resource files were inspected; the full study was not rerun, nor was resource use throughout the original run independently certified.

GPT3.note: Includes the 200 conservatively failed reserved slots in the externally terminated batch; these are not evidence that 200 physical trials actually ran.
